m:nyhavn: Free to walk around at any time. The restaurants with menus on the canal are aimed at tourists and are very expensive: for a proper meal, move a few streets away. Canal boat tours also leave from here (about 200 kroner, about €27, price from a secondary listing: check at the ticket office).
m:christians: Royal Reception Rooms 120 kroner (about €16), ruins, royal kitchen or stables 60 kroner each, combined ticket 175 kroner (prices from tourist listings, not the official website, which was being updated). Under-18s go free. Until 1 November the rooms are open every day 10am–5pm (official website). From 2 November sources disagree about Mondays: to be safe I treat Monday as closed here. Closed on 24 and 25 December. The tower is free but you need a timed ticket, collected at the visitor centre, and ID. The rooms may close without notice for state ceremonies.
m:amalien: The square can always be seen, for free. Amalienborg Museum 125 kroner online and 135 at the desk (about €17–18, from the museum website). From 1 November to 23 December it's closed on Mondays and open 10am–4pm; in October it's normally open every day 10am–4pm (hours to be confirmed). Closed on 24 and 25 December. The changing of the guard at noon is the most striking moment; the time may change when the royal family isn't present, check the Royal Guard website.
m:rosenb: From the official website: open every day 10am–5pm until 1 November; from 2 November to 23 December closed on Mondays and open 10am–4pm. Closed on 24 and 25 December. Last entry half an hour before closing. The ticket costs about 140–150 kroner (about €19–20; prices from tourist listings disagree, I didn't read the official one); online entry costs 5 kroner less. The surrounding park is free and open to all.
m:rund: Entry 60 kroner (about €8); under-18s go free (from the Copenhagen museums website). In the winter period (from 24 November) it's open every day 10am–6pm; I couldn't find the autumn hours, so I use the same. Closed on 24 and 25 December and 1 January; there are also closures for restoration in the winter months: check rundetaarn.dk.
m:tivoli: Entry 200 kroner (about €27), rides extra with a 269-kroner wristband (from a 2026–27 tourist listing: check tivoli.dk). Halloween season from 2 October to 1 November, opening at 11am; closed from 2 to 12 November; Christmas season from 13 November to 3 January 2027. Evening closing time changes from day to day: here I use 10pm, but check the calendar on the website. Closed from 4 January to 18 March.
m:natmus: From the official website: open every day 10am–5pm from April to October; from November to March closed on Mondays. Closed on 24, 25 and 31 December. Ticket 150 kroner at the desk and 135 online (about €18–20). Under-18s go free. The ticket is valid for a year.
m:kastell: Kastellet and the Little Mermaid are free to see at any time, day or night. The paths are open to everyone; the military buildings inside are still in use. Just before, near Kastellet, is the large Gefion Fountain, with the goddess driving her oxen.
m:christiansh: The neighbourhood and the canals are free to see. The church tower is paid (price and hours not checked: see vorfrelserskirke.dk) and closes in strong wind, rain or ice. Christiania is free to enter but there are rules: no photos on the main street (Pusher Street), no running, and respect the people. Pusher Street is an area where illegal drugs are sold: avoid it.
m:torve: Open every day with long hours (usually from 10am into the evening). Here I use a cautious 10am–5pm window for weekdays and holidays; actual hours are longer, but I didn't read them on the website. Almost everything is paid by card.
m:glypt: About 125 kroner, about €17 (price from a secondary listing, to be confirmed on glyptoteket.dk). Usually closed on Mondays and open from 11am to 6pm; on Thursdays it's open into the evening. Hours not checked on the official website: check before you go.
vd:torvehal: The glass covered market near Nørreport: dozens of stalls with smørrebrød, fish, cheeses, pastries and coffee. Everyone takes what they like and eats at shared tables or outside on the square.
vp:torvehal: A sandwich or a dish is between €9 and €16, a pastry with coffee about €7–9 (menu not seen). Hours indicative, to be confirmed.
vd:hallernes: A stall inside Torvehallerne that makes smørrebrød, the typical Danish open sandwich of rye bread with herring, prawns, roast beef or eggs, topped with sauces and garnishes. Eat standing up or at the market's little tables.
vp:hallernes: A piece costs about €5–8 and two are enough for lunch (menu not seen). Hours indicative, to be confirmed.
vd:norden: A café with big windows on the corner of Nikolaj Plads, on the pedestrian Strøget: breakfasts, cakes, simple Danish dishes and a bar. Sit down and watch people go by.
vp:norden: Breakfast costs about €11–15, a dish €16–22 (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:laglace: Denmark's oldest pâtisserie, open since 1870: a display of cakes, the cream and seasonal fruit cake (Sportskage) and hot chocolate. The rooms are 19th-century; sit down or buy to take away.
vp:laglace: A slice of cake with coffee is around €10–13 (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:schonnemann: An 1877 restaurant devoted to smørrebrød, with dark wood rooms and tables near Rundetaarn: order two or three open sandwiches (herring, prawns, roast beef) and a small glass of aquavit. Lunch only, Monday to Saturday.
vp:schonnemann: Two or three open sandwiches cost about €25–40 in total (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed: best to book.
vd:atelier: A small, bright café near the Rosenborg gardens, famous for breakfasts (eggs, avocado, rye bread and pastries) and light lunches. There are few tables, but the queue moves quickly.
vp:atelier: Breakfast costs about €10–15 and a light dish €12–17 (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:paludan: A café-bookshop near Rundetaarn: walls of books from floor to ceiling, wooden tables and a simple kitchen with sandwiches, salads, soups and cakes. Also open in the evening.
vp:paludan: A sandwich or a salad is about €12–16, a soup or dish of the day €14–18 (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:europa: The café on Amagertorv square, on the pedestrian Strøget, with outdoor tables and a great view of the square and the stork fountain. Coffee, croissants and light sandwiches.
vp:europa: A coffee with a pastry is around €8–11 (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:wilder: A neighbourhood café in Christianshavn, on a side street near the canals: American breakfasts, sandwiches, salads and weekend brunch, in a casual setting.
vp:wilder: A brunch or lunch is about €11–17 (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
cd:frelsers: The external spiral tower: 400 steps up to a viewpoint over Christianshavn.
cx:frelsers: Closed in strong wind or ice.
cd:designmuseum: Danish design: chairs, lamps and objects from the 18th century to today.
cd:canal: An hour from Nyhavn through the canals, past the Little Mermaid and the Opera.
cd:carlsberg: The history of Danish beer, with a tasting.
cd:bluplanet: Northern Europe's largest aquarium, with a huge circular tank.
cx:bluplanet: It's in Kastrup, about 9 km from the centre.
cd:zoocph: One of Europe's oldest zoos, with a Norman Foster elephant house.
cd:cisternerne: An underground cistern with art installations in the dark.
cd:hirschsprung: The golden age of Danish painting, in a neoclassical building next to Østre Anlæg park.
cd:experimentarium: The science museum with a thousand hands-on experiments.
cx:experimentarium: It's in Hellerup, about 6 km from the centre.
